title: Intestinal lipid absorption
journal: American Journal of Physiology. Endocrinology and Metabolism
funder: This work was supported in part by National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases Grant DK-46700 and a Grant-in-Aid from the American Heart Association to M. M. Hussain.
result: Narrative review. Pancreatic lipase, with colipase and bile salts, acts on the sn-1 and sn-3 positions of triacylglycerol and releases 2-monoacylglycerol and free fatty acids; 2-monoacylglycerol is the predominant form in which monoacylglycerol is absorbed. In enterocytes, monoacylglycerol acyltransferases join monoacylglycerol and fatty acyl-CoA to diacylglycerol, and DGAT1 and DGAT2 form triacylglycerol, which is incorporated into apoB48-containing chylomicrons in an MTP-dependent manner. Vitamin E occurs as tocopherols and tocotrienols that vary in biological activity owing to differences in bioavailability; its absorption requires micelles, involves SR-BI and occurs mainly through chylomicron secretion.
